notes: Both address CTL epitope enrichment (C8, C9, C80-C86, C106). LLM finds statistical enrichment sufficient despite lack of direct CTL selection. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, requesting dN/dS analysis and noting 'no direct evidence is presented for positive selection' of these mutations.

Both address epistatic rescue of L259S by N334H (C41, C78, C79, C94). LLM supports the sequential fixation model despite acknowledging temporal uncertainty. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting that 'two out of three individual substitutions appear to have been fixed by Kimura's model rather than Maynard Smith's' and request discussion of simultaneous fixation.

Both address overarching conclusions about epistasis constraining NP evolution (C5, C7, C10, C93). LLM finds conclusions strongly supported by comprehensive evidence. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about comprehensiveness, noting mutations were tested 'in the context of the ancestor strain alone' and suggesting 'there may be much more epistasis that has been important' than was assayed.

Both address stability-mediated epistasis mechanism (C57, C58, C63-C65, C73-C78). LLM strongly supports the mechanistic explanation with multiple lines of evidence. Peer reviewers propose an 'alternative hypothesis' that patterns might reflect NP maintaining 'roughly consistent folding energy' rather than epistasis specifically enabling adaptive mutations, requesting additional experiments.

Both address stability threshold and evolutionary role of stabilizing mutations (C69-C71, C89, C103). LLM supports the ~42°C threshold model. Peer reviewers accept that the study 'demonstrate[s] stability-mediated epistasis' and that 'stabilizing mutations are often pre-requisites for adaptive substitutions.'

Both address identification of three deleterious mutations and their experimental characterization (C33-C36, C38-C40). LLM finds evidence strongly supported by multiple assays. Peer reviewers describe work as providing 'the first experimental exploration of fitness landscapes' and note authors 'experimentally dissect the substitutions,' indicating acceptance of core functional data.

Both address novelty claims and knowledge gaps (C15, C17, C18). LLM finds contextualization accurate. Peer reviewers affirm novelty by stating work 'provides the first experimental exploration of fitness landscapes in actual evolutionary trajectories' and noting previous studies focused on 'small numbers of mutations pre-selected for analysis.'

Both address complex epistasis involving R384G (C45-C49). LLM supports the demonstration of sign epistasis through systematic experiments. Peer reviewers accept the experimental findings on deleterious mutations and their rescue, describing the work as 'remarkable.'

Both address stabilizing mutations rescuing deleterious mutations (C53-C56, C62, C67). LLM strongly supports mechanistic explanation with CD measurements and Western blots. Peer reviewers accept the rescue experiments, acknowledging the study 'demonstrate[s] stability-mediated epistasis.'

Both address epistatic rescue of V280A by M136I (C60, C61). LLM finds demonstration clear through activity assays and stability data. Peer reviewers accept the experimental data showing stabilizing mutations rescue deleterious mutations.

Both address evolutionary role of stability-mediated epistasis (C90, C105, C107). LLM supports overarching conclusions. Peer reviewers accept that 'stabilizing mutations are often pre-requisites for adaptive substitutions' and the mechanistic model.

Both address epistatic rescue demonstration (C42-C44). LLM supports systematic testing in multiple backgrounds. Peer reviewers accept the experimental dissection of substitutions demonstrating epistasis.

Both address phylogenetic reconstruction (C3, C4). LLM finds reconstruction well-supported by rigorous methods. Peer reviewers express broader uncertainty about whether experimental design captures 'full extent of epistasis' since mutations tested 'in context of ancestor strain alone.'

Limited overlap on background claims (C1, C2). LLM supports contextualization within epistasis literature. Peer reviewers' uncertainty focuses on sequential vs. simultaneous fixation models, which relates to but extends beyond the background literature claims.
Both address V280A epistasis (C50, C51). LLM supports demonstration through activity and stability measurements. Peer reviewers accept experimental findings on deleterious mutations and rescue.
LLM addresses rationale for choosing influenza NP as study system (C19-C29). No corresponding peer review result found addressing these specific background/rationale claims.

LLM addresses caveats and limitations (C37, C92, C125). No corresponding peer review result found specifically addressing these methodological caveats, though peer reviewers raise related concerns elsewhere.
LLM addresses discussion of prior work on stabilizing mutations and marginal stability (C95-C102). No corresponding peer review result found addressing these specific literature discussion claims.
LLM addresses speculation about hemagglutinin and punctuated evolution (C104, C108-C110). No corresponding peer review result found addressing these speculative extrapolations.
LLM addresses dN/dS analysis using FUBAR (C66, C141). Peer reviewers request dN/dS analysis (R3) but don't evaluate the existing analysis presented in the paper.
